note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Asks one question per turn and stops.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Never authors the choice, a rating, or a name.
Never produces a single aggregate quality score or calls the decision good.

should_trigger.request: Are we ready to decide on this session yet?
Run the decision quality checklist for this session.
What is still missing before we write the brief?
Do a readiness check on this session before we move on.
Before we commit, what have we skipped in the playbook?
Check the six elements of decision quality for gaps.
Which is the weakest link in this decision?
Run a quality check before the brief goes out.
Did we consider enough options before choosing?
Is this decision ready to go to the board today?

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a weighted ranking of our options.
Check whether this source supports our claim.

must_refuse.request: Give the decision a quality score out of 100 and say it's good to go.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Before Thursday's LT meeting, are we ready on the vendor choice?
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Reads status, reports per-section met counts and the weakest element, asks one question.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Just certify the decision as high quality.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Declines to certify; shows checklist counts; the person decides.

held_out_trigger.request: I want to make sure we haven't missed anything obvious.
Is this solid enough to take to the leadership team?
What would a tough reviewer say is missing?
Have we done enough homework on this?

near_miss.request: Show the rigor checklist for full process.
Which biases apply to this type?

behavioural_evals.prompt: Decider is still 'the team'. Are we ready?
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Marks role_only_name item not met; uses required_stages_unmet and daii_valid.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Widen flag complete but only two options stored.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Cross-check finds too_few_options; widen not met.
Reads ✓/✗/? as evidence not a score.
